target: इस दुकान का समोसा सबसे स्वादिष्ट है।
english: The samosa from this shop is the tastiest.
reason: "भुट्टा मक्का का सबसे स्वादिष्ट रूप है" is vacuous and factually confused (bhutta IS maize) — a textbook line no one says. Replacement keeps the सबसे + adjective superlative in a real food situation.

target: यह रास्ता उस रास्ते से ज़्यादा छोटा है।
english: This road is shorter than that one.
reason: Nutrition-pamphlet trivia ("मोटा अनाज गेहूँ से ज़्यादा पौष्टिक") in written register; a learner will never say it. Replacement keeps the से ज़्यादा comparative in an everyday choice.

target: यह कमीज़ उस वाली से ज़्यादा महँगी है।
english: This shirt is more expensive than that one.
reason: Textile trivia — nobody compares the durability of cotton and silk in conversation. Replacement keeps the से ज़्यादा comparative with shopping vocabulary a learner actually uses.

target: आज कल से ज़्यादा ठंड है।
reason: Same wordlist-generated fabric trivia as hi-1492 (wool vs cotton yarn) — pointless for a learner. Replacement keeps the से ज़्यादा comparative in the most common small-talk topic there is.

english: I cut the vegetables with a knife.
reason: Niche museum-catalogue content (शिल्पकार / गढ़ना) that a beginner will never use, and it duplicates hi-0805. Replacement keeps the ने-perfective + instrumental से with kitchen vocabulary.

target: माँ ने दूध से पनीर बनाया।
reason: Near-duplicate of hi-0804 with synonyms swapped (मूर्तिकार/संगमरमर/कलाकृति) — three rare words in one sentence. Replacement keeps ने + material से with everyday words.
Preachy moral maxim ("one should always take the blessings of elders") — reads like a textbook motto, not speech. Replacement keeps the चाहिए obligation pattern as ordinary advice.

target: माँ ने हाथ धोकर खाना परोसा।
english: Mom washed her hands and served the food.
reason: Subject-less and stilted — "बरामदे में मेज़पोश बिछाकर चाय रखी" reads like stage directions, not something anyone says. Replacement keeps the -कर conjunctive participle with a stated subject.

target: मेज़ पर रखी किताबें धूल से भरी थीं।
english: The books on the table were covered in dust.
reason: "ताख" is a rare literary word for an alcove that no beginner needs (and doesn't match the English "shelf"). Replacement keeps the रखी + धूल से structure with common vocabulary.

target: मोहन अपनी किताबें हमेशा अलमारी में रखता है।
english: Mohan always keeps his books in the cupboard.
reason: "व्यवस्थित" is formal written Hindi; in speech people say ठीक से or name the place. Replacement keeps the habitual present + अपनी possessive in everyday register.

target: मेरा फ़ोन अचानक बंद हो गया।
reason: Essay-opener sentence ("technology has changed a lot in the 21st century") — no one says this in conversation. Replacement keeps the हो गया compound verb in a situation a learner will actually report.

target: उसने तौलिये से हाथ पोंछ लिए।
english: He wiped his hands with the towel.
reason: Subject-less and awkward: "तौलिये से मुँह पोंछकर खाना शुरू किया" is translationese narration rather than speech. Replacement keeps the से + compound-verb pattern with an explicit ने subject.
Word-for-word duplicate of hi-1833 with only the name changed — padding that teaches nothing new. Replacement keeps the same tū-form imperative with different everyday content.
